title: Speech on a Galaxy S23 Ultra: what actually ran
reader_must_learn: Which routes produced complete phone speech, and which stopped before inference.
Whether synthesis kept up with playback: RTF below 1 means faster than real time.
CPU versus HTP is meaningful within a named workload, not as a cross-model league table.
Fast or valid audio is not necessarily good speech; listening approval belongs to an exact sample.
HTP needed prepared deployment derivatives; CPU orchestration remained part of the system.
rtf_note: RTF is measured wall time divided by emitted audio duration. At 0.5, ten seconds of audio takes five seconds to produce. Lower is faster; below 1 beats real time. Setup inclusion and workloads are labeled separately.
grouping_rule: Print the named group and its boundary above its rows. Never rank or draw shared-length bars across groups. Chapter observations compare configurations, not isolated providers.
listening_scope: Sample accepted means Moritz accepted that row's exact retained WAV, identified in the cited registry or additive review. It is not family-wide quality, numerical parity, or acceptance of final app output.

numbers_needing_a_caveat: Different groups use different texts, graphs, profiling and lifecycles. No overall winner, shared bars, cross-group speedup ratios or common-scale ranking.

Short Supertonic HTP and chapter HTP are rewritten/non-bit-exact routes whose strict numerical gates remain failed despite exact-sample listening acceptance. Neither is untouched-model FP32 arithmetic.

Chapter RTFs above are explicitly DERIVED with the preferred matched process-entry-to-WAV-close boundary. The source's generation-only RTFs are 0.536596 CPU and 0.417628 HTP, but exclude CPU upfront setup while retaining HTP interleaved setup; do not substitute them without relabeling.

Chapter timings are one first run per configuration, CPU profiled versus HTP unprofiled, with different geometry/lifecycle and later noise divergence. They are not warm medians or a controlled pure-provider speedup; offline preparation is excluded.

About 210 seconds is the emitted chapter audio length, NOT generation latency. The corresponding generation intervals were about 112.7 seconds CPU and 87.8 seconds HTP; process-entry totals were about 113.6 and 88.4 seconds.
VibeVoice's 9.1 GB is package size, not measured RAM, an OOM event or proof the model family cannot fit. Its incomplete-prefix RTF is deliberately not shown as complete-speech performance.

0037 is not yet in this TTS registry snapshot: its two registry_ids arrays are honestly empty. Their committed experiment comparison and additive exact-WAV review are the authority; do not invent registry IDs or transfer earlier short-sample verdicts.
All acceptance labels bind only to the cited exact reviewed outputs. A completed run, good ASR coverage or a CPU sample does not accept another backend, later app output or a model family.
speed_presentation_recommendation: Use plain two-decimal RTF values with warm/first labels, a persistent lower-is-faster note, and visible named workload/boundary headings. Show blocked/incomplete as words, never zero. No shared bars, heatmap or fastest-first sorting across unmatched groups. Keep registry/source links in details. If ten rows feel heavy, move both first-chapter rows to the long-form story rather than mixing their numbers into the short benchmarks.
